clue.text: Book title people misread as "The Careless Shepherdess"

definitions.text: Book title people misread as "The Careless Shepherdess"

parts.words: Book title people misread as "The Careless Shepherdess"
parts.note: the nursery-rhyme girl who lost her sheep is a careless shepherdess; the 'book title' sends you looking for a novel

explanation.surface: A librarian notes that readers keep getting the name of a pastoral novel wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: The nursery rhyme tells of a little girl who lost her sheep; a shepherdess who loses her flock is careless, so the playful alternative title fits her.
explanation.definitionFit: The nursery-rhyme heroine famously mislaid her flock, so a jokey retitling would call her careless with her sheep.

clue.text: More recently one's left on the side

parts.note: something happening more recently happens later
one is A, as in 'a' single thing; the 's is the joining 'is'

explanation.surface: Someone notes that, lately, a person has been left on the sidelines.
explanation.definitionFit: Lateral describes something placed at or toward the side, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Slogan could be eg Latin

indicators.note: could be says these letters might be rearranged into something else

explanation.surface: A motto, it is suggested, might be written in Latin, for example.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could be' rearranges the seven letters of EG LATIN.
explanation.definitionFit: A tagline is a catchy advertising phrase, essentially a slogan.

clue.text: Martin's followers reform most of unearthly laws ultimately

indicators.note: to reform is to reshape, so the letters gathered here are rearranged
most of drops the final letter of the word unearthly
ultimately picks out the final letter of laws

explanation.surface: Followers of some reformer seek to overhaul odd, otherworldly rules.
explanation.walkthrough: 'most of' trims unearthly to UNEARTHL; 'ultimately' adds S from laws; 'reform' rearranges UNEARTHLS.
explanation.definitionFit: Martin Luther founded the Protestant church whose members took his name, so they are his followers.

clue.text: This might be used to mask part of execrable epithet

definitions.text: This might be used to mask

indicators.note: part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A censor's tone would cover a portion of a foul insult.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters sit across 'execraBLE EPithet'; the whole clue also describes what the tone does to a swear word.
explanation.definitionFit: Broadcasters cover swear words with a short electronic tone, masking the offending language.

clue.text: Ram climbing upland gets crushed

indicators.note: in a down entry climbing means the word for ram is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: a tup is a ram, a male sheep
a down is a stretch of rolling upland, as in the South Downs of England

explanation.surface: A ram scaling the hills ends up flattened.
explanation.walkthrough: A tup is a British word for a ram; downs are open chalk hills in southern England.
explanation.definitionFit: Put down means squashed or quelled, as a rebellion is crushed.

clue.text: Opening in Italy European actor interpreted sexy literature

indicators.note: interpreted suggests a fresh reading, so the letters gathered are rearranged
the opening of a word is its first letter, here of Italy

explanation.surface: At a premiere in Italy, a continental actor performs racy writing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'interpreted' rearranges I, E and ACTOR.
explanation.definitionFit: Erotica is writing or art intended to arouse, so it is sexually charged reading matter.

clue.text: He questions prison over traces of Ecstasy and LSD in bread

indicators.note: in a down entry over puts the first piece above the next

parts.note: someone who pumps a person for information is a pumper
nick is British slang for a prison or police station

indicators.note: traces of takes just the first letter of Ecstasy and of LSD

explanation.surface: An interrogator questions a jail about drug traces found in a loaf.
explanation.walkthrough: To pump someone is to question them persistently, so a pumper is one who questions.
explanation.definitionFit: Pumpernickel is a dense dark German rye loaf, a kind of bread.

clue.text: Strait-laced, yet high and inebriated

parts.note: up can mean high, as in raised up
tight is informal for drunk

explanation.surface: Someone prim and proper is paradoxically both stoned and drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: Uptight describes someone stiffly conventional and tense, much like a prudish, rigid person.

clue.text: Dines in café where broken seat's in the open

indicators.note: something broken is in pieces, so the letters are reassembled

parts.note: the word seat, with the 's as a joining 'is'
out means outdoors, in the open air

explanation.surface: A diner sits outdoors at a café on a damaged chair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broken' rearranges SEAT to give EATS.
explanation.definitionFit: To eat out is to have a meal at a restaurant or café rather than at home.

clue.text: New hospital threatened changes immediately

indicators.note: changes says the letters gathered here are altered into a new order

parts.note: H is the map abbreviation for hospital

explanation.surface: A newly built hospital, under threat, is reorganised.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changes' rearranges N, H and THREATENED.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means at that very moment, without delay, i.e. at once.

clue.text: Piggy's loose in last of maize crop

definitions.note: an informal adjective meaning like a pig, matching the adjective answer

indicators.note: loose letters are not held in order, so they are rearranged
last of takes the final letter of maize

explanation.surface: A pig has got free among the last of the cornfield.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loose' rearranges IN, E (from maize) and CROP.
explanation.definitionFit: Porcine means relating to or resembling swine, the formal synonym of piggy.

clue.text: Expectation for Scrooge, say, is incomplete

parts.note: pro means in favour of, i.e. for

indicators.note: incomplete says the word for Scrooge loses its final letter

parts.note: Scrooge, the Dickens skinflint, is an example of a miser

explanation.surface: What one anticipates for Scrooge is left unfinished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'incomplete' cuts MISER to MISE.
explanation.definitionFit: Promise is grounds for expecting future success, as in a player showing promise.

clue.text: Small trench revealed when top of grating's removed

indicators.note: top of points at the first letter of the word for grating
removed says that first letter is taken away

parts.note: a grille is a grating; the 's is the joining 'is'

explanation.surface: A little ditch appears once the drain cover is lifted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'top of' and 'removed' strip G from GRILLE.
explanation.definitionFit: A rille is a narrow channel or furrow, especially on the Moon, so a small ditch.

clue.text: First class crude tanker's carrying one engine valve

parts.note: A1 means first-rate, written AI

indicators.note: carrying says the rearranged letters hold the next piece
crude means rough and unrefined, so the letters are reworked

parts.note: the word tanker; the 's is a joining 'is'
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A top-notch oil tanker contains a vital engine part.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crude' rearranges TANKER into RNTAKE, which 'carrying' wraps round I. 'Crude' also suggests oil, fitting the tanker.
explanation.definitionFit: An air intake is the opening through which an engine draws in air, a valve-like inlet.

clue.text: Locals tear around district on Sunday

indicators.note: in a down entry on means placed above, so the Sunday letter comes after
around says the word for tear surrounds the next piece

parts.note: a rent is a tear or rip
a side can be a district of a city, as in the East Side

explanation.surface: Townsfolk rampage through their neighbourhood on a Sunday.
explanation.definitionFit: Residents are the people who live in a place, i.e. the locals.

clue.text: Advantages in winding streets

indicators.note: winding streets twist about, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: There are benefits to living among twisting lanes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'winding' rearranges STREETS into TERESTS.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting in someone's interests means for their benefit, so interests are advantages.

clue.text: Note the Parisian company's starting to manipulate transmission of information

parts.note: te is a note of the sol-fa scale
le is French for 'the'
CO is the abbreviation for company; the 's is a joining 'is'

indicators.note: starting to takes the first letter of manipulate

explanation.surface: A French firm sets out to control the flow of news.
explanation.definitionFit: Telecom, short for telecommunications, is sending messages over distance by wire or radio.

clue.text: Be very pleased about Irish writer's broadcast

parts.note: re means about or concerning

indicators.note: broadcast means put on air, so the writer's name is heard, not seen

parts.note: James Joyce, the Irish author of Ulysses

explanation.surface: Delight greets a radio programme about an Irish novelist.
explanation.walkthrough: JOICE is how the name of James Joyce sounds.
explanation.definitionFit: To rejoice is to feel or show great joy, so to be delighted.

clue.text: Find room for some of it inside

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Make space for a portion of something indoors.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters sit across 'oF IT INside'.
explanation.definitionFit: To fit in something is to find space or time for it in a schedule or place.

clue.text: If sense is modified tact ensues

indicators.note: modified means altered, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: If one's wits are adjusted, diplomacy follows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'modified' rearranges IF SENSE.
explanation.definitionFit: Finesse is delicate skill in handling people or situations, close to diplomacy.

clue.text: Being upset I tot up runs and stop working

indicators.note: being upset means being overturned, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A cricket scorer gets annoyed totting up the runs and quits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Being upset' rearranges I TOT UP plus R.
explanation.definitionFit: A circuit breaker or machine that trips out cuts off and ceases to function.

clue.text: Austere knight's delight following misfortune

definitions.note: an adjective here, while the answer is a noun for a grim spoilsport, used attributively

indicators.note: following says the word for delight comes after the misfortune

parts.note: K is the chess abbreviation for knight; the 's is a joining 'has'
ill means harm or misfortune
joy is delight

explanation.surface: A stern knight takes pleasure only after bad luck.
explanation.definitionFit: A killjoy spoils others' fun, the sort of stern, severe, unsmiling person who frowns on pleasure.

clue.text: N Americans are jerks!

definitions.meaning: slang for people from the United States
pulls sharply, a verb in the third person

explanation.surface: Exclaims that North Americans are idiots.
explanation.definitionFit: Yanks is informal for Americans, and yanks means tugs abruptly.

clue.text: He might fill hollow with bit of silver in it

parts.note: a dent is a hollow or depression

indicators.note: in places that letter inside the word it
bit of takes only the first letter of silver

explanation.surface: Someone plugs a cavity using a piece of silver amalgam.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes the job: filling a cavity with silver amalgam.
explanation.definitionFit: A dentist fills cavities in teeth, so he is someone who might fill.

clue.text: Choice to omit first reading

indicators.note: to omit first says the opening letter is dropped

parts.note: an election is a choice, as in a vote

explanation.surface: A person elects to skip the opening reading.
explanation.definitionFit: A lection is a passage of scripture read aloud in a church service.

clue.text: Without musical arrangement, leaders of Northern Concert Orchestra rose in revolt

indicators.note: in revolt means turning over, so these letters are rearranged
leaders of takes the first letters of the three following words

explanation.surface: An orchestra's principal players mutinied when no sheet music arrived.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in revolt' rearranges NCO plus ROSE.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacking a score means having no written music, so no orchestration.

clue.text: Unravelled, St Peter's ministry, lacking special effort, is not enduring

indicators.note: unravelled means tangled threads pulled apart, so these letters are rearranged
lacking says some letters of the jumble must be left out

parts.note: a try is an effort or attempt

explanation.surface: The ministry of St Peter falls apart without any particular endeavour.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove S and TRY from the letters of ST PETERS MINISTRY, then rearrange the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Impersistent is a rare word meaning transient, the opposite of lasting.
